chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, who said:

Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about a young goat that suckled from the milk of a sow until it grew and became mature. Then a man used it as a breeding male among his flock, and offspring came from it.
He عليه السلام said: “As for what you know specifically from its offspring, do not approach it. But as for what you do not know, it is in the same position as cheese, so eat and do not ask about it.”

key_terms.اسْتَفْحَلَهُ: he used it for breeding as a male
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْجُبُنِّ: treated like cheese, meaning not investigated beyond apparent permissibility

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the offspring of a goat that drank the milk of a sow?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about the offspring of an animal affected by nursing from a sow. What is specifically identified as descending from that animal is to be avoided, while what is not identifiable is treated under the principle of permissibility without further inquiry.
